beschreibung: Psychological counseling is not psychotherapy – but counselors encounter people with psychological distress and disorders every day. This module explains what constitutes a mental disorder, how the ICD-11 is structured, and how common clinical pictures and warning signs can be recognized. A particular focus is on the limits of counseling and on responsible referral.
lernziele: You can explain what is understood by a mental disorder and describe the main features of the ICD-11.
You can name the core features of depression, anxiety disorders, trauma-related disorders, and addictive disorders.
You can apply the vulnerability-stress model to case examples.
You can recognize warning signs of suicidality and other acute crises and address them appropriately.
You can name the legal and professional limits of psychological counseling and handle a referral responsibly.

pruefung.frage: Which statement about the vulnerability-stress model is correct?
optionen: Mental disorders arise exclusively from genetic factors.
Mental disorders arise from the interplay of individual susceptibility and current stressors.
Stressors play a role only in people without vulnerability.
The model applies exclusively to anxiety disorders.
pruefung.erklaerung: The model according to Zubin and Spring emphasizes the interplay of vulnerability and stress. It is applied to almost all mental disorders and supplemented by protective factors.

pruefung.aussage: Complex post-traumatic stress disorder is included in the ICD-11 as a diagnosis in its own right.
pruefung.erklaerung: Complex PTSD (6B41) was newly introduced with the ICD-11. It comprises the core features of PTSD as well as disturbances in self-organization.

pruefung.frage: Which of the following belong to the three core features of PTSD according to the ICD-11? (Multiple answers possible)
optionen: Re-experiencing the trauma in the here and now
A persistent sense of current threat
pruefung.erklaerung: The ICD-11 describes PTSD in terms of re-experiencing, avoidance, and a persistent sense of current threat. Euphoria and delusions are not part of it.

pruefung.frage: According to learning theory, what contributes most strongly to the maintenance of anxiety disorders?
pruefung.erklaerung: Avoidance and safety behaviors bring short-term relief but prevent the corrective experience that the feared catastrophe does not occur.

pruefung.aussage: According to the state of research, directly asking about suicidal thoughts increases the risk of suicide.
pruefung.erklaerung: There is no evidence for this widespread assumption. Addressing the topic openly makes an assessment possible and is often experienced as relieving by those affected.

pruefung.frage: A client reports that he has a concrete plan to take his own life tonight and has already obtained the means. What is the appropriate response?
optionen: Not leaving him alone and calling the emergency number 112 or arranging immediate emergency care
Giving him the number of the TelefonSeelsorge (German telephone crisis line) and making an appointment in two weeks
Changing the subject so as not to burden him further
Explaining to him that he has to think of his family
pruefung.erklaerung: Concrete plans and preparations signify acute danger. The person must not be left alone; immediate emergency care is required. The other options leave the acute risk unaddressed or come across as moralizing.

pruefung.frage: Which features does Ringel’s presuicidal syndrome describe? (Multiple answers possible)
pruefung.erklaerung: Ringel described constriction, inhibited aggression or aggression turned against oneself, and suicidal fantasies. Increased sociability and planning for the future tend to argue against a presuicidal syndrome.

pruefung.frage: Under the Heilpraktikergesetz (German Non-Medical Practitioners Act), which activity is prohibited for persons without an Approbation (state license) or a Heilpraktiker license?
optionen: Accompanying people in a career decision
Providing information about regional support services
pruefung.erklaerung: Diagnosing, curing, or alleviating illnesses – including mental illnesses – constitutes the practice of medicine (Heilkunde). Accompanying people with life questions, providing information, and conducting conversations are, by contrast, core components of counseling that does not involve the practice of medicine.
